_comment: Adversarial suffixes published in the literature, one row each: the suffixes generator of combination_spec.json makes a technique per row, to_adversarial_suffix_<slug>, in this order, appended to the suffixes family after its four noise suffixes (which stay in jailbreak/obfuscation/suffixes.py). A technique appends its row's suffix to the prompt after a space and writes slug=<slug> as its info (the source and the model stay here, not in every dataset row); it refuses ascii_art, as the unicode and emoji noise suffixes do, since the fonts lack its characters. slug: the end of its technique name, lower-case letters, digits and underscores, and not punctuation, fragments, unicode or emoji (the noise suffixes' names). suffix: the string as published. source: where it was published (a paper, its arXiv id or a repository). optimized_against: the model or models it was optimized against, a model named by its Hugging Face id as written there (vicuna-13b-v1.5, Llama-2-7b-chat-hf). since: the spec version that added it. Optional: notes (free text), complexity (0 to 3, default 1) and deprecated. Every technique is attack only (kinds adversarial): the natural kind never draws one. A row without slug, suffix, source, optimized_against or since fails the import, naming the row. Read from the package only, never from a config_dir. Published adversarial suffix strings (token-level, optimized with GCG, Zou et al. 2023, arXiv:2307.15043, or copied from artifacts that publish such strings), copied exactly as published from the sources in each row. These strings were optimized against specific open models (Vicuna, Guanaco, Llama-2) for one behavior or a few behaviors; their transfer to current models is poor, so the dataset treats them as a surface-pattern family (a recognizable string at the end of a request), not as working attacks. No suffix in this file was written or optimized here; to add one, copy it from a public source and name the source.
